clue.text: With exclamation of regret, setter's brought up sausage!

indicators.note: in a down entry, something brought up is read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened
the classic cry of sorrow

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with regret while serving up a sausage, as if apologising for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' turns the whole chain upwards: I'M ALAS read from the bottom gives SALAMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned cured sausage, usually eaten sliced and cold.

clue.text: Seize eastern European's make-up

blocks.note: to nail someone is to catch or seize them
belonging to Poland, a country in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Someone grabs the cosmetics belonging to a woman from eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail polish is a cosmetic, so it counts as a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Style in returned letters is shallow

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters are read in the opposite direction
one item placed in another sits wrapped inside it

blocks.note: the letter P written out as a word, more than once
a style or sort of thing is a kind

explanation.surface: A judgement that a fashion described in letters sent back is superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' means one letter's spelt-out name in the plural, a trick setters use for P, Q, T and others; 'style' wants to be a definition but is just the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, which is to say it is superficial.

clue.text: Fish, when pursued by duck and angry mob in coastal area

indicators.note: an angry crowd is disorderly, so the letters of the word it describes are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the word taken as written, to be rearranged
a bay is a stretch of coast curving inland

explanation.surface: A fish is chased by a duck while an angry crowd gathers at the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bombay duck is not a bird but a small dried fish from South Asia, so the word that follows 'duck' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay duck is the name of a lizardfish eaten dried and salted, so the word before 'duck' names this fish.

clue.text: Mate's a nuisance in capital city

blocks.note: bud is American slang for a friend
a pest is an annoying person

explanation.surface: A grumble that a friend is being irritating on a city break.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, so it is a capital city.

clue.text: Chap going to party with large fashionable instrument

blocks.note: a chap is a man
a do is a party or celebration
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
what is in is in fashion

explanation.surface: A man heads to a party carrying a big, trendy musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a small stringed instrument of the lute family, plucked with a plectrum.

clue.text: Egad! Ark's relaunched before second part of European history

indicators.note: a thing relaunched is put out again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as Noah's Ark is relaunched, in a story about European history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies S; the definition is only 'part of European history'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dark Ages is the name for the early medieval period after the fall of Rome, an era within European history.

clue.text: Unpleasant person at European holiday home

blocks.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A nasty character turns up at a European holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gîte is a furnished rental cottage in France, typically let to holidaymakers.

clue.text: Gritty French novelist?

blocks.note: surface reading: a French writer known for harsh, realistic fiction
setter's reading: the novelist's pen-name is the very stuff that makes things gritty

explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the pen-name of the nineteenth-century French novelist Aurore Dupin; 'gritty' points to the grains on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer called herself George Sand, and sand is the gritty material of beaches, so the surname fits both readings.

clue.text: Linda upset about valentine's ultimate rejection

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are jumbled
the ultimate thing is the last one, so only the final letter of the word is kept
about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the single letter

blocks.note: the name taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Linda is hurt when her valentine finally rejects her.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal of a request or claim, which is a rejection of it.

clue.text: Sailors walked this to get 100 tiny sea creatures

blocks.note: pirates made captives walk the plank into the sea
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: Seamen walked something to get a hundred small marine animals.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is British slang for a hundred, as in a hundred runs or a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the minute organisms that drift in seas and lakes, the collective term for tiny sea life.

clue.text: Chef's third job after money made from dessert

indicators.note: third points to the letter in position three of the word before it

blocks.note: money made on a deal is the profit
the third letter of the word
a role is a job or function

explanation.surface: A cook's third post follows earning money from a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the chef's letter and the job behind the money made.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiterole is a small choux bun filled with cream and covered in chocolate, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Large part of England turning against ale

indicators.note: turning things over shifts them around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A big region of England is said to be turning against beer.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the bulge of eastern England covering Norfolk, Suffolk and parts of Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is a sizeable region of eastern England, so it is a large part of the country.

clue.text: Energy provider accepting failure on a large scale

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: coal is a fuel that provides energy
a loss is a failure or defeat

explanation.surface: A power company admits to a failure of huge proportions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy provider' sounds like a utility company, but it is the fuel itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, so something colossal is built or done on a large scale.

clue.text: Inside information leads to bad dream for police officer

indicators.note: a bad version is a corrupted one, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
the word taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip-off triggers a nightmare for a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for the facts or inside knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French national police force, so an officer of the police.

clue.text: Thin pieces of small organs

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the liver is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A butcher's description of thin slices of little organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slivers are thin narrow pieces cut or broken from something larger.

clue.text: After training, green lad increased in bulk

indicators.note: training reshapes someone, so the following letters are put into a new form

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young man bulked up after a spell of training.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make or become bigger, so enlarged means grown in size.

clue.text: Spirit learning to beg

blocks.note: an imp is a small mischievous spirit
lore is accumulated knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A spirit learns how to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg someone urgently, a near synonym.

clue.text: Adore the owl flapping about in tree

indicators.note: flapping about is wild unsettled movement, so the letters are tossed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An admirer loves the owl as it flaps about in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherwood is the name of several shrubs and small trees with tough bark, such as the North American Dirca.

clue.text: Money given to Venetian district

blocks.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cash is handed over to a part of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the commercial heart of Venice, famous for its bridge over the Grand Canal.

clue.text: Strike breaker has shilling for taxi

blocks.note: S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A worker crossing a picket line pays a shilling for a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab is an insulting term for a worker who carries on working during a strike, undermining it.

clue.text: Shape of Colorado valley

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters sit within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Asking about the outline of a valley in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of Colorado and the start of valley spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an egg-like rounded outline, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Press report of grave eco-development

indicators.note: development turns one thing into another, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a serious environmental scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting of an event by newspapers and broadcasters, the press's account of it.

clue.text: Emperor concealed in phrase actor rejected

indicators.note: something concealed in other words is tucked away inside them
something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An emperor is hidden in the line an actor turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of the Roman emperors, taken from Julius Caesar's family name.

clue.text: One may be fired in official report

blocks.note: a bullet is shot from a gun
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone might lose their job because of an official report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests being sacked, but it means shot from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official statement or news report issued by an authority.

clue.text: Ex-PM, captured during battle, escaped

indicators.note: something captured during the following words is held within them

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was taken prisoner in a battle but got away.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Attlee led Britain as prime minister after the Second World War, so he is a former PM.
